minutes_text:
CITY OF TEMPLE CITY AND
  TEMPLE CITY UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT
  STANDING COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES

  THURSDAY, APRIL 9, 2026

1. CALL TO ORDER

  The meeting was called to order at 4:00 p.m. at the Temple City Unified School
  District Conference Room at 9700 Las Tunas Drive, Temple City, California.

2. ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:  Board Member Georgino, Board Member Smith,
  Superintendent Cunha, Assistant Superintendent Wu, and
  Executive Assistant Montero

  Councilmember Chavez, Mayor Man, City Manager Cook,
  Public Safety Supervisor Amaya, and Administrative
  Assistant to the City Manager and City Council Ortiz

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF JANUARY 15, 2026

  Mayor Man made a motion to approve the Minutes from January 15, 2026.
  Seconded by Councilmember Chavez.

  Action:  Approved.

4 . DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. CITY AND SCHOOL DISTRICT UPDATES

  City Update

  I. E-Bikes
  • Public Safety Supervisor Amaya reported on the city’s efforts to
  educate residents about e-bike safety during the Neighborhood
  Watch meetings. He also shared that the California Highway
  Patrol offers a free online training program that the city can share
  with the school district.
  • The City will continue working with the school district on education
  efforts, especially at the start of the school year. This includes
  conducting another bike rack check, with support from the
  Sheriff’s Department, to ensure students are following the rules.
  II. Traffic Analysis Longden Elementary
  • City Manager Cook reported that engineers are currently
  analyzing traffic patterns at Longden Elementary, with a draft of

  recommendations expected within the next week for the school’s
  review. Further discussions will take place between the city and
  the school and district before implementation.
  • Parking signage is expected to be replaced before the end of the
  school year.
  Temple City Unified School District Update
  I. Safe Routes to School
  • City Manager Cook reported that no new funding is currently
  available; however, the City will continue exploring road
  improvement opportunities throughout the city.
  • Superintendent Cunha requested information regarding the left
  turn on Lemon and Temple City Boulevard. City Manager Cook
  will follow up with information from the engineers’ report.
  II. Camino Real Landscaping
  • Superintendent Cunha requested assistance with the
  beautification and asked about alternative options for improving
  the curb to sidewalk area.
  • Mayor Man responded that the City will explore funding
  opportunities to support these enhancements, including options
  such as drought resistant improvements.
  III. School Ballot Measure
  • Superintendent Cunha reported that polling results were favorable
  for the proposed measure, which will be a bond focused on safety,
  infrastructure,  and  Career Technical Education (CTE)
  improvements.
  • A resolution for the measure will be presented to the school board
  for approval in July, with the measure anticipated to appear in the
  November ballot.

  B. DISCUSSION FOR FUTURE MEETINGS

  The topics discussed during the meeting, including e-bikes, traffic analysis
  at Longden Elementary, safe routes to school, Camino Real Landscaping,
  and the school ballot measure will be agendized for further discussion at
  the next meeting.

  Superintendent Cunha asked that solar energy at schools be added as a
  topic on the next agenda.

  5.  UNFINISHED BUSINESS - None.

  6.  CLOSING COMMENTS/QUESTIONS (COMMITTEE MEMBERS) –

  Mayor Man thanked the school district for including the City Council in the
  Edison Scholar scholarship presentation.

  8.  SCHEDULE NEXT MEETING DATE

  The next meeting is scheduled to be held on Thursday, July 23, 2026, at 4:00
